fact: Egypt's Ministry of Transport added a digital accessibility service to its website mot.gov.eg with text-to-speech, speech-to-text, a sign-language interpreter, dyslexia fonts, a reading mask and keyboard navigation, working with the ICT ministry and the National Academy of IT for Persons with Disabilities.

fact: The Ministry of Transport says it continues to develop its website and the websites of its affiliated authorities and companies for inclusion.

fact: Egypt's ICT ministry launched accessibility tools on its official website, including screen-reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, font and contrast changes and an accessibility icon, available on all pages.

fact: The article says a presidential initiative to strengthen digital accessibility of government websites, implemented by the National Academy of IT for Persons with Disabilities, aims to generalise accessibility standards across government bodies' sites.
system: Presidential initiative on digital accessibility of government websites

fact: Egypt's NTRA, with the Central Bank, issued instructions requiring mobile operators to make e-wallet services accessible to people with disabilities, with sign language interpreters, Braille contracts and mobile apps with audio interfaces, voice dictation and screen reader support.
NTRA previously established a sign language complaint service via video calls on its website.
system: NTRA sign language video-call complaint service

fact: The Central Bank of Egypt says it issued a dedicated regulation requiring banks to make banking services accessible to persons with disabilities, including screen reader compatibility on bank websites, Braille forms, sign-language video calls, and audio and sign-language versions of bank information and brochures.
system: CBE regulation on accessibility of banking services for persons with disabilities
